search_bias_seed.bias: start outside mainstream agent literature; prioritize optimization, operations research, autonomous experimentation, distributed systems, and information-efficient resource allocation; require quantitative mechanism evidence before proposing transfer
search_bias_seed.seed_description: Quantitative primary-source-first queries were intentionally centered on non-agent mechanisms and then translated inward only after evidence extraction.

candidates.mechanism: Adaptive capping during automatic algorithm configuration: stop evaluating a candidate as soon as its accumulated cost is already worse than the incumbent, and use repeated configuration search over structured parameter/component spaces.
quantitative_evidence: ParamILS reported general SPEAR optimization speedups of 20x on SWV and 1.3x on BMC; instance-specific optimization yielded over 500x on SWV and 4.5x on BMC.
For SWV, the best configured SPEAR solved every instance within 20 seconds versus multiple one-CPU-day timeouts under original defaults.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: For expensive agent/system variants, maintain an incumbent and terminate a trial once a conservative lower bound on remaining attainable score cannot compensate for consumed cost. Combine with automated search over orchestration, memory, tool, verifier, or curriculum knobs. This is stronger than naive fixed-budget sweeps because evaluation cost becomes endogenous to observed trajectory quality.
candidates.scope_limits: Evidence is from SAT/MIP-style algorithm runtime configuration; direct transfer requires agent metrics with safe monotone or statistically bounded early-stop criteria. Non-monotone learning curves can make aggressive capping discard late-blooming candidates.
candidates.evidence_strength: high for source domain; medium transfer confidence

candidates.mechanism: Successive-halving / Hyperband: sample many configurations cheaply, repeatedly discard poor performers, and allocate progressively more resource only to survivors.
quantitative_evidence: Hyperband observed 6x-70x speedups over random search in studied settings; its paper reports over an order-of-magnitude speedup over competitor sets on varied deep-learning and kernel problems.
The authors note a roughly 50x maximum speedup over random search under their linear-resource settings, but measured 70x where training scaled superlinearly with resource.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: Use staged evaluation ladders for candidate architectures/policies/prompts: cheap microbenchmarks and short rollouts first, then progressively more realistic and expensive evaluations for surviving candidates. This directly targets research-loop throughput rather than only final-model performance.
candidates.scope_limits: Hyperband was weak where per-trial startup overhead dominated and where low-fidelity performance poorly predicts full-fidelity performance; these failure modes must be measured before transfer.
candidates.evidence_strength: high for source mechanism; high relevance to expensive evaluation loops

candidates.mechanism: Cost-aware multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization: explicitly model both objective quality and evaluation cost as functions of fidelity, then select the next low/high-fidelity evaluation by expected information gain per cost.
quantitative_evidence: FABOLAS reported finding high-quality SVM and DNN hyperparameter solutions 10x-100x faster than state-of-the-art Bayesian optimization methods or Hyperband in its experiments.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: Instead of a fixed fidelity ladder, choose dynamically among synthetic tests, small task subsets, short horizons, smaller models, or reduced tool budgets according to expected decision information divided by cost. This can reduce false economy from spending too much on cheap but uninformative proxies.
candidates.scope_limits: Requires calibrated correlation between fidelities and the target objective; surrogate misspecification can bias selection toward misleading cheap evaluations.
candidates.evidence_strength: high source-domain evidence; medium-high transfer confidence

candidates.mechanism: Closed-loop Bayesian active learning: after every experiment, update beliefs and choose the next experiment that maximizes useful information or expected improvement rather than following a static grid.
quantitative_evidence: CAMEO reported a 10-fold reduction in required experiments for phase mapping/material discovery, with iterations taking tens of seconds to tens of minutes.
A mobile robotic chemist ran 688 experiments over eight days in a 10-variable space and found photocatalyst mixtures six times more active than initial formulations.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: Treat research/evaluation questions themselves as experiments. Maintain uncertainty over competing mechanisms and choose the next benchmark, ablation, adversarial test, or environment to maximally discriminate hypotheses instead of simply accumulating more average-case scores.
candidates.scope_limits: The 10x result is materials-specific and includes physics-informed priors; the robotic-chemist sixfold improvement is objective improvement, not a direct experiment-count speedup. Transfer requires an explicit hypothesis/uncertainty representation and reliable experiment outcomes.
candidates.evidence_strength: high source-domain evidence; medium transfer confidence

candidates.mechanism: Tail-tolerant tied/hedged requests: after a small delay, issue a duplicate to an independent replica and cancel the loser; combine with fine-grained dynamic load balancing.
quantitative_evidence: In a BigTable/file-system benchmark, a tied request after 1 ms reduced median latency by 16% and 99.9th-percentile latency by 38% on a mostly idle cluster; under concurrent terasort, reductions were 21% median and 32% at the 99.9th percentile.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: For high-variance reasoning/tool trajectories, start a duplicate only when a trajectory becomes a latency outlier, then cancel the loser. This may reduce time-to-first-valid-answer or long-tail evaluation stalls at much lower cost than unconditional N-way sampling.
candidates.scope_limits: This mechanism improves latency/tail robustness, not reasoning quality by itself. Benefit depends on sufficient independence between replicas and low cancellation/duplication overhead.
candidates.evidence_strength: high source-domain evidence; medium transfer confidence

promising_unverified.mechanism: Optimal Computing Budget Allocation (OCBA): allocate repeated noisy simulations disproportionately to alternatives most likely to affect best-design identification.
promising_unverified.reason_pending: A project summary states comparable simulation quality with one-tenth the simulation effort, but this run did not yet pin that exact figure to a directly inspected primary paper. Keep out of high-confidence feed until primary quantitative verification.

promising_unverified.mechanism: Statistical racing: eliminate configurations as soon as repeated-instance evidence establishes inferiority; restart sampling distributions to avoid premature convergence.
promising_unverified.reason_pending: Mechanism is well documented, but this run did not extract a clean primary quantitative efficiency result comparable across tasks.
